observed_vs_expected: The expected quarter-wave convergence (35–45 nm for HfO2, 45–55 nm for SiO2) is not yet met; observed thicknesses span broadly from 53.00 nm to 126.50 nm across all four candidates. Valid candidates (9) successfully exceed the >5 expectation, and tightest_margin (0.4098) remains strongly positive, confirming the design stays within manufacturable bounds. As this is the first round, best_target_score (0.5606) serves as a baseline and does not yet reflect cumulative improvement.
deviation_mechanism: The lack of quarter-wave clustering is a transient exploratory artifact, not a physical failure. At λ=300 nm, optimal quarter-wave optical thickness requires ~39.5 nm for HfO2 (n≈1.90) and ~51.7 nm for SiO2 (n≈1.45). The current population clusters heavily near 90–120 nm, which corresponds to half-wave optical paths. Half-wave layers introduce net-zero phase accumulation per period but break the alternating high-low impedance contrast needed for constructive interference at the band center. With only one evaluation cycle, selective pressure has not yet collapsed the distribution from these broader initial conditions into the narrow quarter-wave resonance windows.
continue_rationale: Fewer than two rounds have executed, mandating continuation per protocol. The route remains scientifically productive: valid_candidates=9 demonstrates a well-populated search space, and tightest_margin=0.4098 confirms robust structural feasibility. The current thickness dispersion (53–126 nm) reflects early-stage sampling. Additional rounds will supply the necessary optimization cycles to drive layers toward their respective quarter-wave optima and produce measurable score advances relative to the 1e-4 epsilon reference.
insight_for_next: Restrict thickness initialization bounds to 30–50 nm for HfO2 and 40–60 nm for SiO2, seeding new candidates centered on λ/(4n) = 39.5 nm and 51.7 nm respectively. Apply a temporary increase in step-size/mutation intensity for the first two rounds to rapidly shift the population out of the 90–120 nm detuned region, then taper perturbation magnitude as scores improve to fine-tune toward exact quarter-wave conditions.
insight_grounding: Current population exhibits systematic optical-path over-thickness: candidate 0 layer 0 measures 90.80 nm, candidate 3 layer 0 measures 95.38 nm, and candidate 1 layer 3 measures 119.0 nm. These values sit 2.3×–2.5× above the theoretical 37.5–39.5 nm HfO2 quarter-wave target and >2× above the 51.7 nm SiO2 target. This specific multi-layer detuning forces premature phase wrapping that suppresses peak reflectivity/transmission at 300 nm. Pinning initialization to the calculated λ/(4n) windows directly eliminates the dominant phase-error source identified in these exact measurements.
